description.value: A First Nation-operated RV park and campground at Witset on the Yellowhead Highway beside the Bulkley River, with solid cycle-tourer amenities including showers, laundry, and device charging; the famous Witset Canyon salmon weir is a short walk from camp.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies this as an RV park and campground operated by Witset First Nation, with tags for tents, showers, laundry, Wi-Fi, power, toilets, and dump station. The website at witset.ca/camping exists and confirms the name 'Witset RV Park and Campground' in the page title, but the camping page itself contains no facility details whatsoever — it is essentially a placeholder. The About page confirms Witset is a Wet'suwet'en village 30 km west of Smithers. Because the website provides no campground facility information, I cannot confirm any amenities beyond what OSM tags suggest, and per the rules OSM amenity tags alone are not authoritative, so amenities remain null.
concerns: The camping page at witset.ca/camping is essentially a placeholder with no facility details, making it impossible to verify any amenities from the website.
OSM address (159 Telkwa High Road) differs from the website footer address (#3 - 205 Beaver Rd) — the footer address is the Band Office, not the campground itself.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, operating campground accepting tents and RVs, operated by Witset First Nation along the Highway 16 cycling corridor between Smithers and Hazelton. A useful stop for touring cyclists.
enrichment_extras.notes: Formerly known as Moricetown Campground. OSM tags suggest showers, laundry, Wi-Fi, power hookups, toilets, and a dump station, but none could be confirmed from the website content.

wow_evidence: First Nation-operated… showers, laundry, and device charging; the famous Witset Canyon salmon weir is a short walk from camp
